note: Read by arrangement. The first source; its guards are the ones every other source inherits. The id is boyceville, NOT bigriver-boyceville: the id is the output filename (data/<id>.json) and data/boyceville.json is what the Emmert Worker reads. Renaming it would disconnect both sites silently. COORDINATE CORRECTED 2026-08-20. The previous pin was the TOWN, not the elevator: 45.0642,-92.0248 sits 4.1 km from the yard. The value now here was cross-checked against the operator's own published street address and geocoded independently by the US Census geocoder and the ArcGIS World GeocodeServer, which agree to within 137 m of the Census point for N10185 370th St. It came from a list of Sig's own earlier basis1st project, whose high-precision rows were sampled eight ways on 2026-08-20 and came back facility-accurate seven times out of eight, median 123 m from the operator's published address -- close enough to tell Allied's Auburndale East site from its West site 3.2 km away, and United's Beaver Dam grain site from its corporate office 6.5 km away. A pin six kilometres out is the difference between the right answer and the wrong one when a farmer asks which elevator is nearest.
inMergeWhy: Barchart already carries Boyceville, and more fully (beans plus a second corn program). Read for the Emmert sites, which consume data/boyceville.json directly; excluded from the AGSIST map so one elevator is not two rows.
routesNote: MORE THAN ONE WAY TO THE SAME NUMBER -- 2026-09-18. This board had exactly one route: the url above, asked three times with the same method and the same headers. One layout change, one 403, one bad DNS answer and there was no other attempt at a price sitting in public. These are now RACED rather than walked: the url above starts first and gets a head start to itself, and each route below starts 1500ms after the one before it if nothing has answered yet. The FIRST answer whose board passes every guard wins and the rest are aborted, so an ordinary day still makes exactly one request and publishes exactly what it publishes today, while a primary that has gone quiet costs about a second and a half instead of the whole pass. `trust` is how sure anybody is that the URL serves this board: `verified` means it was read off a real capture of their page or is this manifest's own, `inferred` means it is derived from how this vendor's platform behaves on OTHER hosts this project reads successfully, or that a page this project fetched named it without this project ever asking it. bigriverbids.com could not be reached from the sandbox these were derived in -- the egress proxy answers 403 to CONNECT -- so NOT ONE of them below has been confirmed against the real host. None is described here as known-good. GATED 2026-09-18 AND UNGATED THE SAME DAY. The fallbacks were briefly held behind a failure count and an hour of sustained failure and the run was capped at sixteen requests. The owner, who holds the arrangement, has said he wants no throttle and as much redundant scraping as this repository can manage, so every route is available on every pass. What is left is a wall-clock deadline, ROUTE_BUDGET_MS, which exists so a black-holed host cannot wedge a pass that fires every ten minutes. `tier` below still records where a route came from, because that is true and worth knowing; it decides nothing. See lib/routes.mjs.

routes.why: The same path on the www spelling of the same host. dnilgis/bids adds the apex/www twin to every source it reads (lib/sources.mjs urlsFor) and its poller tries it whenever the bare host fails, because one of the two failing DNS is not the elevator being down; test/multisource.test.mjs asserts that twin for THIS url by name. The hostname is not a guess: on 2026-09-08 urlfinder asked bigriverunitedenergy.com, was redirected, and 283 KB came back with a 200 from the bigriverbids host -- recorded in its ledger and reconstructed in test/urlfinder.test.mjs with the landing url https://www.bigriverbids.com/. That observation was at / and not at this path, so what is established is that the host answers, not that this exact URL does.

Dyersville's own page. The URL is verbatim in fixtures/bigriver-2121.html, a real capture of their board -- Dyersville in their own nav -- so the page exists. What is INFERRED is that it carries Boyceville's rows: one page on this platform holds every location as a tab panel, which is why filterLocation and locationId exist at all, and the 2121 capture demonstrably carries panels keyed 2162 and 2165 beside its own. Boyceville's rows are keyed 2121 and nothing else on the page is published, so a page that does NOT carry them refuses with 'none for location 2121' rather than publishing Dyersville's. Tier break-glass: this is not the arranged URL. That is a note about where the route came from, not a gate -- it is raced with all the others on every pass.

Monmouth's own page, on the same evidence as 2162: the href is verbatim in the capture, and the capture's third rendered panel is keyed 2165, so Monmouth and Boyceville are demonstrably served by one page in at least one direction. Two siblings rather than all six: they are the two whose panels were captured beside Boyceville's, and a third adds nothing the first two do not already cover. Tier break-glass: this is not the arranged URL. That is a note about where the route came from, not a gate -- it is raced with all the others on every pass.

arrangement: READ BY ARRANGEMENT, AND ONLY ONE URL IS ARRANGED. `url` above is that URL: one page, one location, read for the two Emmert sites. bigriverbids.com is robots-disallowed to crawlers -- dnilgis/bids records it in scripts/urlfinder.mjs line 91, with THE ONE ARRANGED URL exempt -- so every entry in `routes` that is not `url` is a path this project has no arrangement for. THAT IS RECORDED HERE AS HISTORY, NOT AS A GATE. On 2026-09-18 the owner, who holds the arrangement, said he does not want the fallbacks throttled or limited: Big River publishes this price for the public to read and he wants as much redundant reading of it as this repository can manage. So every route is raced on every pass. `tier` still says which a route is -- `alias` for the arranged path at another spelling of the arranged host, checked as one by lib/routes.mjs, `break-glass` for everything else -- because a year from now the difference between 'the arranged page under another name' and 'a URL somebody added' is worth being able to read off the file. routesFor() still refuses a route that does not declare its tier and still refuses one that records no evidence for itself. Neither check limits when a route runs.
